title: DeepSeek Says It Isn't Optimizing for Users or Revenue
hook: Reported remarks from a four-hour investor meeting: DeepSeek's founder frames products as one rung on the ladder to AGI, and treats commercial restraint as a deliberate strategy.
key_points: A Chinese write-up compiled 52 remarks attributed to founder Liang Wenfeng from a four-hour investor meeting.
The stated central objective is AGI, not maximizing returns through products.
Products are described as one rung on the path to AGI, not something to spend much energy on.
DeepSeek has always been commercializing, per the remarks, but commercialization is not the objective.
A full pivot toward commercialization is said to be still very far away, with restraint framed as a strategy.
This is a community summary of a compiled secondhand account — treat the specific wording as reported, not verbatim.
content_html: A Chinese article compiled 52 remarks attributed to DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng from a four-hour investor meeting, and an English summary circulated widely. The strategic picture it paints is unusual for a lab of DeepSeek's profile: user growth and revenue are explicitly not the target.
extra_html:
The stance

Per the remarks, DeepSeek has one central objective — AGI — and this is not the moment to maximize returns through products. Products are a rung on that ladder, not a destination, and the lab reportedly doesn't intend to spend much thought or energy on consumer or enterprise offerings. It has always been commercializing, the account says, but commercialization is not the objective, and the point at which the company fully pivots toward it is probably still very far away. Restraint, in this framing, is itself a strategy rather than an absence of one.

How much to trust it

Three layers separate a reader from the speaker: a private meeting, a compiled Chinese write-up, and a community translation and summary. Individual sentences are not safe to quote as verbatim policy. What's worth holding onto is the direction — a frontier-capable lab publicly declining the growth-and-monetization playbook its Western peers are running — because that stance, if real, shapes what DeepSeek ships and what it open-weights. Summarized on r/LocalLLaMA, July 2026.
